_about: What the rest take's model happened to write, remarked on where it is read (build_storyboard.py, REST_NOTES; "p<i>" after passage i, counted without the judges' letters). Rewritten for each retake. Take: build/rec_rest3, up to the job menu.
p1: Empathy notices that her clothes are subtly wrong for a farm, in a way it cannot pinpoint. That is this mind's eye: it reads how a person sits in their place. Nothing in the rules backs it up; take it as the character's own impression.
p4: Diligence judges the act by its own measure, and slips in its creed: the joint on the side nobody sees is as good as the one they do. And doing it taught a new way of thinking, Social Interaction, which from now on can write replies too.
p7: Nautical Jargon talks like a sailor, even in a barn: strong as a mast. Odd minds make odd replies, and some of the best moments in a run come from them.
p13: Her answer drifts into her own pride: they laugh at her ideas, and copy them two springs later. Read it as a farmer who has outlasted every doubt about her farm.
advice_asking: My advice: when a conversation matters, pick replies written by your strongest minds. Their levels become dice in that final roll.
job_done: The conversation was the hard part. The job itself is just a menu.
